signals.title: NZD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Geopolitical Tension
signals.text: The G10 scorecard shows JPY leading the complex with a 1W average of +1.473% across 7 pairs, while NZD lags as the weakest currency at -1.079% across 4 pairs, creating a wide 2.552% spread. Strait of Hormuz escalation headlines reporting a blast and targeted tanker drive WTI crude up 3.88% to $96.6, supporting JPY across crosses despite VIX printing contained at 16.5. NZD positioning shows specs heavily net short at -23,004 contracts (Williams pctl 4, z -1.81), yet the currency continues to bleed lower against regional peers. Meanwhile, NZD/JPY BEER misvaluation sits severely stretched at z = -3.29σ (spot 90.09 vs fair value 93.82). The RBNZ OCR overnight rate of 2.75% provides a +177bp carry advantage over BoJ TONA at 0.98%, but geopolitical headlines and JPY domestic data outperformance (ESI +28.7 vs NZD -1.7) dominate the flow. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/JPY; momentum and bilateral divergence override the positive carry advantage. Catalyst: Next high-impact New Zealand macro release. Risk: De-escalation headlines in the Middle East trigger immediate mean-reversion toward BEER fair value.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Downside Hedging + Yield Decoupling
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 153.54, sitting entirely below its SMA20 (158.45), SMA50 (160.16), and SMA200 (158.43) moving-average cluster. Saxo 1M 25-delta risk reversals print at an extreme -2.31 put skew, demonstrating heavy institutional demand for downside protection even as 1M ATM implied volatility sits at 10.8% against HV30 of 11.3% (negative VRP of -0.5%). CFTC positioning reveals leveraged funds expanded net short JPY contracts to -111,297 (pctl 2, z -2.18) following a massive WoW liquidation of -29,678 contracts. Cross-asset correlation between USD/JPY and US 10Y yields has broken to +0.045 against the 252-day norm of +0.333 (z = -1.62σ), proving that US Treasury yield spikes fail to support the pair. While Fed SOFR at 3.65% vs BoJ TONA at 0.98% still provides a +267bp carry advantage to the dollar, retail positioning at 86% long signals heightened contrarian flush risk. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY; severe options put skew and correlation breakdown point to sustained downside pressure. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 18 Sep — hike bias priced. Risk: Rebound back above the SMA200 at 158.43 invalidates immediate downside continuation.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Long + Retail Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7220, holding above its SMA20 (0.7151), SMA50 (0.7054), and SMA200 (0.6995) bullish cluster. Leveraged funds hold +50,250 net long contracts (week ending 2026-09-01), marking an extreme 94th percentile (z = +1.79σ) of its 52-week historical distribution, while WoW delta stalled at -3,328 contracts. This institutional crowding sharply diverges from retail sentiment, where Myfxbook shows 91% short positioning fading the rally. RBA AONIA at 4.35% vs Fed SOFR at 3.65% provides a +70bp carry premium supporting AUD, while Australia's Economic Surprise Index stands firm at +17.3. However, BEER fair value model flags spot as rich at z = +1.78σ (fair value 0.7099), while Saxo 25d risk reversals maintain a modest put skew of -0.52. Trade bias: Long AUD/USD; institutional positioning and carry favor upside but retail capitulation risk demands caution. Catalyst: RBA meeting 29 Sep — hold priced. Risk: Leverage fund net positioning turns negative, confirming speculative exhaustion into resistance.
evidence: RBA 4.35% vs Fed 3.75% — 60bp AUD carry premium

signals.title: EUR/USD — ECB Policy Meeting Ahead of SMA Cluster
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1636, holding tightly between its SMA20 at 1.1619, SMA50 at 1.1520, and SMA200 at 1.1638. Leveraged funds reduced short exposure with net contracts at -52,784 (Williams pctl 31, z -0.39) following a +20,265 contract rebuild over 4 weeks. Fed SOFR at 3.65% vs ECB €STR at 2.19% maintains a +146bp carry spread favoring USD, while nominal policy rates stand at Fed 3.75% vs ECB 2.40% (+135bp spread). Saxo 1M implied volatility trades at 5.0% vs HV30 of 4.6% (+0.4% VRP), with 25d risk reversals nearly flat at -0.11, indicating an options market waiting for direction. Eurozone ESI at +5.5 confirms mild positive macroeconomic surprise momentum ahead of Thursday's policy decision. Trade bias: Neutral EUR/USD; macro carry deficit counterbalances the technical base above SMA20. Catalyst: ECB rate decision 10 Sep — hike priced. Risk: ECB holds rates and delivers a dovish statement, triggering a break below the SMA50 at 1.1520.

signals.title: USD/CHF — Options Volatility Compression at SMA Cluster
signals.text: USD/CHF prints at 0.8101, trading directly through its SMA20 (0.8074) and SMA50 (0.8088) while maintaining position above the SMA200 at 0.7933. Saxo 1M ATM implied volatility registers at 6.9% against 30-day realized volatility of 8.1%, generating an extreme negative volatility risk premium of -1.2%. This vol complacency emerges despite Fed SOFR at 3.65% vs SNB SARON at -0.04% creating a massive +369bp carry buffer in favor of the dollar (Fed 3.75% vs SNB 0.00% nominal spread of +375bp). Leveraged funds sit net short CHF at -12,346 contracts (pctl 16, z -0.93), having shed -2,136 contracts WoW. With the US yield curve in a bear flattener and VIX at 16.5, flight-to-safety flows into the franc remain muted. Trade bias: Bullish USD/CHF; massive structural carry advantage and compressed options pricing favor spot extension. Catalyst: SNB meeting 24 Sep — hold priced. Risk: Realized volatility spike accompanied by a drop below the SMA50 at 0.8088.
